findings.text: _profile_cache_root resolves XDG_CACHE_HOME ahead of RECKON_HOME, so the suite's autouse isolated_reckon_home fixture does not cover this cache whenever XDG_CACHE_HOME is set; the two in-process cases then write foreign-{1..4}.json into the real user cache, and because a nonexistent project's stamp is [None,None] its key is date-stable within a day, so a second same-day run reads those files, never calls the monkeypatched loader, and test_two_picks_read_each_foreign_ledger_once fails on its reads assertion. Reproduced: XDG_CACHE_HOME at one shared temp dir gives 3 passed on run 1 leaving four foreign-*.json files, then 1 failed / 2 passed on run 2 with that id. Fix: order RECKON_HOME ahead of XDG_CACHE_HOME, or point the two cases at a tmp_path cache as the cross-process case already does. Unaffected here because XDG_CACHE_HOME is unset on this workstation.

build() still reads the pick's own project ledger through the uncached run_time_profile (the live path passes no records, so the elif project: branch runs), so a fresh-process pick decodes its own project's ledger once per pick with the new persisted cache not applied there; constant in the number of foreign projects, so it does not defeat the node's goal, but it is the same reusable reading and the natural next cut for the pick's dispatch-bound latency.

raw_text:
VERDICT goal: the node's goal is that a pick reads each foreign project's ledger at most once while the ledgers are unchanged; the change adds a two-layer run-time-profile cache in lane_context (_cached_run_time_profile) -- an in-process memo plus a per-project persisted JSON under a user cache directory -- keyed on a freshness stamp (the aggregate ledger file's mtime+size and the runs directory's mtime) folded with the trailing window's end date, so a repeated pick reuses each foreign project's profile and the expected-wait figure is byte-identical. The goal is met: an independent three-process driver reproduces cold reads all four foreign ledgers, warm reads none, and a mutation removing the persisted read re-reads all four, with expected_wait_s 420.0 in every arm.
VERDICT done_when: the brief's four required behaviours are all present -- the figure still counts every live local worker (the pick's own project from records, each foreign owner from its profile, lane_context.py:468), the cost no longer scales with foreign-project count (persisted reuse across processes), tests/test_picker_foreign_wait_is_bounded.py exists with the three required cases, and the per-phase figures are recorded in docs/evidence/fragments/one-typesafe-model-picker/picker-foreign-wait-bounded.html with the truncated duplicate sentence removed from picker-pick-within-bound.html (range diff -2 lines; grep finds no 'Gate. Base arm and head arm run the picker test files with').
VERDICT write_paths: the reviewed range afec9a9f..830e715 changes five paths, all within the node's declared grants -- reckon/crew/picker/lane_context.py, tests/test_picker_foreign_wait_is_bounded.py, docs/evidence/fragments/one-typesafe-model-picker/picker-foreign-wait-bounded.html, docs/evidence/fragments/one-typesafe-model-picker/picker-pick-within-bound.html and docs/figures/one-typesafe-model-picker/picker-foreign-wait-bounded/foreign-read-cold-warm.png -- and leaves the granted-yet-unchanged run_time_profile.py alone; no plan, sprint or index state was mutated.
VERDICT manifest: read; status complete, base_suite 119 passed exit 0 at afec9a9f and after_suite 122 passed exit 0 at 830e715, negative_control.log 1 failed/2 passed EXIT=1, three commits ce7be6dd8/46d962fe3/830e71586 each conventional with a body and no AI trailer.
VERDICT diff: read afec9a9f against 830e715: 195 added lines in reckon/crew/picker/lane_context.py add _PROFILE_CACHE, _stat_stamp, _ledger_stamp, _profile_cache_root/_path/_key, _read_persisted_profile, _write_persisted_profile and _cached_run_time_profile, and swap the foreign owners' run_time_profile call at lane_context.py:468 for the cached one; plus a 250-line test file and the two evidence fragments and the figure. The expected-wait answer is deliberately unchanged, which the equal expected_wait_s in every arm confirms.
VERDICT call_sites: the cached path is reached from one production call site -- lane_context.py:468 inside _expected_wait, the foreign-owner branch -- with its internal fall-throughs to the uncached run_time_profile at lane_context.py:396 and :404; a separate uncached read of the pick's own project ledger remains at lane_context.py:581 inside build (records is None on the live cli.py path, cli.py:1782).
CALL_SITES: reckon/crew/picker/lane_context.py:468, reckon/crew/picker/lane_context.py:396, reckon/crew/picker/lane_context.py:404
SCORE goal_fidelity: 20
JUSTIFICATION goal_fidelity: the goal is met exactly and independently: a pick now reads each foreign project's ledger at most once while its stamp is unchanged, the answer is identical (expected_wait_s 420.0 cold == warm in my driver and 3325.0 both passes in measure-pick.log), reuse survives across processes (my driver's second process read no foreign ledger, its spy file created empty as a positive control), and a mutation that removes the persisted read restores four reads -- so the reuse is exactly the persisted layer. The figure still counts the pick's own project and every foreign owner.
SCORE evidence: 17
JUSTIFICATION evidence: both arms reproduce under my own re-runs -- head 122 passed exit 0 in the reviewed worktree (module __file__ there) and base 119 passed exit 0 from a fresh git-archive extraction of afec9a9f (module __file__ in the base tree), matching the run's own gate-head.log/gate-base.log, with zero added failures; my independent negative control reproduces the guard. The cut: the two in-process tests are not hermetic -- they rely on the autouse RECKON_HOME fixture to isolate the cache, but _profile_cache_root prefers XDG_CACHE_HOME over RECKON_HOME, so wherever XDG_CACHE_HOME is set they write foreign-*.json into the real user cache and, because the stamp of a nonexistent ledger is date-stable, a same-day second run short-circuits the spy loader (finding below). In this workstation's environment XDG_CACHE_HOME is unset, so the recorded arms are valid here.
SCORE scope_discipline: 20
JUSTIFICATION scope_discipline: the range touches only the five granted paths; run_time_profile.py is in scope and correctly left unchanged (the cache belongs in the picker consumer, as the manifest records); no plan, sprint or index state was mutated; commits are local and conventional.
SCORE durability: 16
JUSTIFICATION durability: the reuse is pinned by three new cases (two-pick reuse of four foreign ledgers, a moved stamp forcing a re-read, and the cross-process case against a shared cache directory whose second process must read nothing), and a red control is recorded and independently reproduced by me; every commit carries a conventional subject and a body with no AI trailer. The cut: only the cross-process case sets its own cache directory, so it is the one robust pin; the two in-process cases can silently short-circuit under a set XDG_CACHE_HOME (finding below), which weakens them as standing pins.
SCORE fit: 19
JUSTIFICATION fit: comments and docstrings state the mechanism and its reason, name no plan, sprint or ticket identifier and carry no author attribution; no live project name appears in the changed source or test (grep clean; the fragment's project ids are evidence data); ruff check is clean on all three changed Python files; no Co-Authored-By trailer on any of the three commits. The one tile is a latent coupling: the persisted file's key folds in the ledger stamp and the window's end date but not the profile's own parameters, which is safe only because _cached_run_time_profile hardcodes the default window.
FINDING reckon/crew/picker/lane_context.py:295 follow-on: _profile_cache_root resolves XDG_CACHE_HOME ahead of RECKON_HOME, so the suite's autouse isolated_reckon_home fixture (tests/conftest.py:610, which sets RECKON_HOME to a temp tree) does not cover this cache whenever XDG_CACHE_HOME is set. The two in-process cases then write foreign-{1..4}.json into the real user cache, and because a nonexistent project's stamp is [None,None] its key is date-stable within a day, so a second same-day run reads those files, never calls the monkeypatched loader, and test_two_picks_read_each_foreign_ledger_once fails on its assert sorted(reads) == sorted(projects). Reproduced: with XDG_CACHE_HOME pointed at one shared temp dir, run 1 is 3 passed and leaves four foreign-*.json files, run 2 is 1 failed / 2 passed with that exact id. This is the repo's 'a test must not read or write state outside the repository under test' rule; the fix is to order RECKON_HOME ahead of XDG_CACHE_HOME, or have the two cases set RECKON_RUN_TIME_PROFILE_CACHE to a tmp_path as the cross-process case already does. In this workstation's environment XDG_CACHE_HOME is unset so the recorded arms are unaffected.
FINDING reckon/crew/picker/lane_context.py:581 follow-on: build() still reads the pick's own project ledger through the uncached run_time_profile (the live path passes no records, so the elif project: branch at :581 runs), so a fresh-process pick decodes its own project's ledger once per pick with the new persisted cache not applied there; this is constant in the number of foreign projects, so it does not defeat the node's goal, but it is the same reusable reading and the natural next cut for the pick's dispatch-bound latency (the run's own follow_ons already note the ~9.7-10.6 s pick). Raising it because it is the one remaining per-pick ledger read on the path this node touched.
